title: Daytime Running Lights (DRL) Trap: Automatic Front DRLs Often Leave Rear Taillights COMPLETELY DARK in Rain, Fog, or Dusk!

no_head_on_same_lane.note: All visible vehicles travel same direction ahead in same lane; no oncoming facing vehicle in same lane.

no_rhd_cabin.note: Driver and steering wheel on left side of cabin in both panels; no right-side steering wheel shown.

single_bulb_signal.note: Roadside signal on right in both panels shows only middle yellow lens lit, top and bottom dark.

us_right_hand_traffic.note: Vehicle travels in right lane with yellow dashed centerline on left and white solid edge line on right.

zero_text.note: License plates are blank gray shapes, no readable letters or numbers; red X and green check are graphic icons, gauges show only ticks/needles with no legible text.

scene_match.note: Split rear-view in fog: left panel car with dark unlit rear vs right panel same car with bright red taillights and headlamp-switch inset OFF vs ON.

result.summary: Split comparison correctly teaches DRL rear-dark trap with correct US lane markings, left-hand drive, and single-lens signal.

teaching_correct.note: Left dark rear vs right illuminated red taillights with switch position clearly teaches to turn headlamps fully ON in low visibility.

result.what_i_see: Two-panel driver-view comparison on a foggy highway following a dark hatchback; left panel shows its taillights completely dark, right panel shows bright red taillights, each with headlamp-switch inset.
